history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration develop a multi-year resource mobilization plan which takes into account emerging donors to raise funds and prevent a liquidity crisis in the Peacebuilding Fund.
history.administration_response: In 2023, the number of donors contributing to the Fund increased to 36, compared to 33 in 2022. Moreover, the percentage of donors with multi-year commitments increased from 24.2 per cent in 2022 to 30.6 per cent in 2023. While 36 donor partners generously contributed $131.8 million to the Fund, contributions are well below the $330 million target and dropped by 22 per cent compared to 2022. With increased demand from Member States despite a decline in contributions, the Fund has reached its lowest liquidity level since its inception and, as a result, lowered its 2024 approvals target from $400 million to $150 million. However, the decision of the General Assembly to provide assessed contributions to the Peacebuilding Fund, starting in 2025, will help bring more predictable and sustainable resources, while an increase in voluntary funding will also remain essential. In 2023, in an effort to demonstrate the impact of the Fund’s efforts to voluntary contributors, working visits by contributing Member States to country level programmes continued. The Assistant Secretary-General for Peacebuilding Support, the Advisory Group and development partners visited Honduras (March 2023), the Democratic Republic of Congo (May 2023), and Mauritania (October 2023). Donor visits to countries supported by the Peacebuilding Fund will continue as needed, in line with the Peacebuilding Fund multi-year resource mobilization plan. The Administration therefore requests closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration has developed the mobilization plan as recommended, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
